chapter_note: Not a proper kephalaion but a framing/justification sequence for the entire work. The oldest teaching layer survives as a compressed cosmogonic survey in paragraphs 1-9, mapping the full cosmic drama from primordial separation through final reintegration. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system — realm structures, cosmic agents, cosmic processes. Heavy lacunae throughout. Paragraphs 10-23 are entirely institutional: Mani asserting scriptural authority, narrating earlier apostles (Jesus, Zarathustra, Buddha), and commanding disciples to preserve his oral teaching — the editorial justification for compiling the Kephalaia. Editorial fatigue is strong (0.67), with substrate vocabulary disappearing completely in the second half while institutional vocabulary doubles. The cosmogonic substrate is genuine but presented in highly compressed summary form, likely an editorial condensation of fuller substrate teaching found in later chapters.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation of the First Man — a core substrate narrative. 'The power came forth from [the Father]' describes cosmic emanation; the First Man arms himself with 'the armour of light' and confronts the enmity. Process-oriented, impersonal, both sides within the cosmic system. The 'crucified it' language is notable — may be older than its Christian overlay.

The numbered structures (three earths, four mountains, three vessels) are the hallmark of substrate enumeration.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Substrate eschatology: the final purification, separation, and reintegration of the divine. 'The fire blazes,' 'he becomes purifier and goes up to his essence' — cosmic process. 'The darkness is gathered in to a bond' — final binding. 'A single God comes to be over the totality' — the restored divine unity. 'You find no opponent' is teaching voice (impersonal second person), not exhortation — it describes the eschatological cosmic state. Both sides of every mapping remain within the cosmic system. The 'You' address is part of the Persian pedagogical tradition.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Very brief substrate fragment about the primordial mixture of light and darkness. 'Mixed and joined with one another' is the substrate description of the cosmic mixture — a core concept that the entire cosmogonic drama addresses. Both sides internal to the system.

Clear institutional layer: Mani enumerating his canonical scriptures (The Great Gospel, Treasury of the Life, The Treatise, The One of the Mysteries, The Writing for the Parthians, Epistles, Psalms, Prayers). 'These three lessons are the measure of all wisdom' — Mani's truth-claim. Institutional score 13.68 — highest in first half. This is the pivot point from cosmogonic substrate to institutional framing.

Institutional score 7.27. Mani's self-assertion: 'Every writer, if he reveals these three great lessons: that one is the writer of truth. Also, every teacher...' First-person truth-claim extending the canonical framework. The 'three great lessons' structure is Mani's own organizational category.

Describes what the 'first great lesson' contains. Some cosmological terms survive in the fragments ('the twelve,' 'the doors that are opened,' 'the four corners') but they are REFERENCED as topics within Mani's lesson structure, not systematically expounded as substrate teaching. 'My pains' and 'my afflictions' are autobiographical — Mani's first person. The cosmological terms are subordinated to the institutional framework.

Flagged as probable editorial extension (high institutional vocabulary 12.3 with register shift). Mani urging disciples to write down his oral teaching — the direct justification for the Kephalaia as a sub-canonical text. 'The teachers,' 'the leaders,' 'the elect and the catechumens' — institutional hierarchy vocabulary. 'The questions that you have asked me' — explicit reference to the Q&A format that will structure the Kephalaia.

Imperative command to preserve teaching: 'You must remember them and write them; gather them in different places.' Institutional prescription — text-preservation directive. Part of the Kephalaia justification sequence.

Institutional score 3.42. Mani describing his differentiated teaching to different audiences: 'The elect [...] psychic wisdom [...] The suckling babes, according to their ability.' 'The sects and the heresies' — reference to contemporary religious landscape, but used here in Mani's biographical narrative rather than as a cosmic→contemporary mapping. Institutional self-description.

Apostolic succession narrative: 'the apostles [...] the earliest fathers past unveiled it in their scriptures.' Mani positioning himself within a lineage. 'The church' — institutional vocabulary. 'In each place, in each city, in each land' — biographical description of mission scope.

Historical narrative about Jesus: 'At the time that Jesus trod [...] the land of the west [...] his parables [...] the signs and wonders.' Apostolic succession — establishing that earlier apostles taught truth but did not write their own scriptures. 'My beloved ones' — direct address to community. Biographical/historical, not cosmological.

Institutional score 5.71. Historical narrative about Zarathustra: 'he came to Persia, up to Hystaspes the king [...] Zarathustra (did not) write books. Rather, his disciples who came after him, they remembered; they wrote.' Apostolic succession pattern: earlier apostle → did not write → disciples wrote after him → teachings adulterated. Specific historical proper noun (Hystaspes).

Highest institutional score in chapter (23.68). Buddha narrative following the same apostolic pattern: 'He chose his churches, and perfected his churches [...] he did not write his wisdom in books. His disciples, who came after him, are the ones who remembered.' 'Churches' used anachronistically for Buddhist sangha — institutional vocabulary imposed on the narrative.

Institutional argument for written scriptures: 'the fathers of righteousness did not write their wisdom in books [...] their righteousness and their church will pass away from the world.' 'Lead astray,' 'adulterate,' 'mix' — vocabulary of textual corruption. This is the editorial argument that justifies Mani's canonical project and, by extension, the Kephalaia.

Institutional score 3.95. Mani's command to write: 'unveiled for you in my scriptures [...] the wisdom and the interpretation [...] you write after me, so that [...] it leads you not astray!' Institutional prescription with protective rationale. 'The commandments' — institutional vocabulary.

Final institutional command: 'remember! And write a little something from the great wisdom that you have heard from me.' Direct address to community with imperative voice. Content is about text preservation, not spiritual exhortation — the voice is exhortatory but the purpose is institutional (preserve the teaching). 'City after city, in each land separately' echoes paragraph 16.

Devotional closure: 'When you write and are amazed by them [...] enlighten greatly; and they shall give benefit and make free [...] of the truth.' Promises spiritual benefit from the act of preservation. This is the wrapper that closes the institutional sequence with a devotional seal. Brief and formulaic.
